newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon issues money supply statistics.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon issues money supply statistics.

text.p: Lebanon's M1 money stock rose 44 billion Lebanese pounds in July to 1,736 billion pounds, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly report on Wednesday.
Its annual growth recorded 22.4 percent relative to July 1995.
M2 rose 383 billion pounds in July registering a 36.32 percent growth over the same month last year, the Bank said.
M3 rose by 723.8 billion pounds in July registering a 2.89 percent monthly increase and a 17.29 percent growth over the same month last year, the Bank added.
M4, a newly-introduced indicator, rose by 818 billion pounds to 29,696 billion pounds, registering a 23.69 percent annual increase.
The Bank issued the following statistics (blns of Lebanese pounds at end of period):
The Bank defined the aggregates as follows:
M1 -- Currency in circulation + Demand deposits
M2 -- M1 + Other deposits in Lebanese pounds
M4 -- M3 + Treasury bills held by the non-banking system
